verdictBasis: 1 blocker, 3 SHOULD-FIX, 1 advisory. ACCEPT was gated at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX.
verdictStatement: Two of my three v5 findings are repaired properly and one is repaired most of the way. OTHER-FSTYPE gains the enum-absent condition, a normalization rule with case-folding, an exact digest input and an exact serialization; the soname companion finally exists as a named optional field with a closed shape inside both libc authenticity payloads; and the inherited coordinator pin's live locator now points at reMeasurementAtV6, whose three values all reproduce against live bytes at the dispatched HEAD. Roster closure holds again — 68 changed leaves, 0 uncovered. But the repair that replaced the Linux identifier scheme introduces a worse instance of the defect it was fixing. linux-distro-userspace is a two-part identifier with no composition rule feeding a single canonicalIdentifier field, it carries no normalization at all in a scheme whose equality rule compares 'byte-exact canonicalIdentifier after normalization', it calls its publisher component closed while closing it nowhere, and it ends in an open 'or equivalent' escape. Two further defects were created by otherwise-good repairs: the fstype token source names a BSD interface that does not exist on Linux, and moving the soname companion inside the compared identityEvidence payload while deleting v5's 'companion labels never decide identity' sentence leaves an optional field governed by an exact-match drift rule.

blockers.title: linux-distro-userspace is not a computable identifier: no normalization, no composition rule, an unclosed 'closed' vocabulary, and an open escape

measurement.theText: observation: 'closed publisher/distribution identifier plus userspace-release (or equivalent PLATFORM-ATTESTED platform-image identity). uname -r alone is not a complete Linux host-ABI profile key.'
measurement.noNormalization: The scheme defines none. I searched the whole artifact: normalization language for the version selector occurs only inside macos-product-build's observation ('after Unicode NFC and trim of leading/trailing ASCII whitespace'). v5's linux-uname-release said 'after the same normalization' and that inheriting clause was deleted when the scheme was rewritten. EXACT-BUILD.equality still reads 'same identifierScheme and byte-exact canonicalIdentifier after normalization', so for the Linux scheme that clause now has no referent.
measurement.noCompositionRule: EXACT-BUILD.requires names a single canonicalIdentifier. The Linux observation describes a two-part value — publisher/distribution identifier plus userspace-release — with no separator, ordering, or serialization rule for rendering the pair into that one field. 'canonicalIdentifier' occurs exactly twice in the artifact, once in requires and once in equality, and is defined nowhere. debian 12.5, debian-12.5 and debian/12.5 are all conforming renderings of one platform and are byte-unequal.
measurement.closureAsserted: The publisher component is called a 'closed publisher/distribution identifier'. No enumeration, publishing source, or vocabulary for it appears anywhere in the artifact. The macOS scheme names its publisher concretely; the Linux one names the property 'closed' and leaves the set empty.
measurement.openEscape: '(or equivalent PLATFORM-ATTESTED platform-image identity)' admits an entirely different identifier form into the same scheme with no bound, so even two parties agreeing on distro and release may produce different lawful values.

blockers.whyThisIsABlocker: supportedVersionOrBuildSelector is a required member of the profile key that gates allowlist freeze, and beforeAllowlistFreeze requires every required member to be populated. Under this scheme two conforming parties cannot compute the same value for the same Linux host on any of four independent axes, so a frozen allowlist is not reproducible for the whole linux half of osFamilyEnum. This is the same class of defect I blocked at CLAUDE-V5-B1 for the filesystem token — the contract claiming to own a grammar it does not author — arriving in the repair that was meant to close it.
blockers.consequence: Fail-closed rather than exploitable: mismatched renderings refuse rather than substitute. But a required member two parties cannot compute alike cannot survive a second verifier.
blockers.requiredRepair: Define the Linux scheme the way the macOS one is defined. Name the observation interface (for example os-release ID and VERSION_ID as a named file publishes them), give the scheme an explicit normalization clause so EXACT-BUILD.equality has a referent, state the exact composition of the two parts into the single canonicalIdentifier, and either enumerate the publisher vocabulary or stop calling it closed. Bound or remove the 'or equivalent PLATFORM-ATTESTED platform-image identity' escape — if it is retained it needs its own tag and equality rule, not a parenthetical inside another scheme's prose.

shouldFix.title: The OTHER-FSTYPE token source names a BSD-only interface, leaving the Linux half of the escape on an unnamed 'or equivalent'

measurement.theText: 'the filesystem-type string as the platform's named statfs/f_fstypename (or equivalent) interface publishes it'
measurement.theFact: f_fstypename is a BSD and macOS struct statfs field. Linux's struct statfs has no such member — its filesystem type is f_type, a numeric magic, and the string form comes from a different source entirely (mount-table interfaces such as /proc/self/mountinfo or /proc/mounts). So for osFamily=linux the named interface does not exist and the whole clause reduces to the unnamed '(or equivalent)'.
measurement.residualDivergence: Two Linux verifiers can legitimately read different string sources for one volume, and the parenthetical also reopens the macOS half since a verifier may substitute any interface it judges equivalent.

shouldFix.whatImproved: Recorded in fairness, because most of CLAUDE-V5-B1 did land. lawfulOnlyWhen restores the enum-absent condition that v5 deleted; normalization is now explicit and includes ASCII case-fold, which absorbs the zfs/ZFS class of divergence I raised; digestEncoding now names the exact hashed input as the UTF-8 encoding of the normalized token; and serialization fixes the emitted shape as exactly { tag: OTHER-FSTYPE, algorithmId, digest }, which also answers the shape ambiguity. The residue is bounded to non-enum filesystems, and on Linux specifically — not the open-ended hole v5 had.
shouldFix.minimumRepair: Name the Linux source explicitly alongside the BSD one, per osFamily, the way schemeBinding now binds version schemes to osFamily. Then either drop '(or equivalent)' or state what makes an interface equivalent.

shouldFix.title: sonameAbi now sits inside the compared identityEvidence payload, but the sentence excluding it from identity comparison was deleted in the same edit

measurement.whatLanded: Both libc-bearing payloads now carry optionalLibcCompanion { field: 'sonameAbi', shape: { soname, abiSelector }, extraFormsRejected: true, notAuthenticity: true }, and the SONAME-ABI entry now carries an encoding pointer to that field. The companion is finally encodable, which was the substance of CLAUDE-V5-S1.
measurement.whatWasDeleted: v5's SONAME-ABI.comparison — 'companion labels never decide identity; authenticity remains the attested or digest-bound object' — is removed at v6. What remains is notAuthenticity: true, which says the field is not authenticity evidence, and a union-level 'never sole authenticity'.
measurement.theContradiction: identityRuleShape.sameMeans makes two objects the same member iff platformProfileKey, class and identityEvidence 'compare equal', and drift is 'any runtime resolution whose identityEvidence is not an exact allowlist match'. sonameAbi is now a field of identityEvidence. Nothing excludes it from that comparison, so under drift's exact-match rule a companion that differs — or that is present on one side and absent on the other — is drift and refuses. A field cannot be both optional and load-bearing for an exact match.
measurement.whyItIsNewAtV6: At v5 the companion had no representation anywhere, so it could not enter the comparison. Moving it inside the compared payload is exactly what made an exclusion rule load-bearing, and that is the edit in which the exclusion rule was dropped.

shouldFix.consequence: Fail-closed and only when a producer actually uses the optional field, but two conforming verifiers can disagree on whether a sonameAbi difference is drift, so one refuses and one matches on the same object.
shouldFix.minimumRepair: Restore an explicit comparison rule on the companion — that sonameAbi is excluded from the sameMeans and drift comparisons and never decides member identity — either on each optionalLibcCompanion object or as a clause in sameMeans.

advisories.title: SONAME-ABI remains a member of identityEvidenceUnion.tags though it is not a tag
advisories.detail: identityRuleShape.identityEvidence.form says every signed entry carries exactly one tag from the classMap for its class, and SONAME-ABI appears in no classMap list. It nevertheless still sits in the tags map beside the two real tags, so a reader building a parser from tags gets three entries of which two are lawful.
advisories.whyOnlyAdvisory: The harm is now nil: the entry carries notASignedEntryField: true, notAuthenticity: true, and an encoding pointer to the sonameAbi field, so no producer can misread it as an identity tag. My CLAUDE-V5-S1 minimum repair offered a defined subfield as one of two acceptable routes and v6 took it; this is the leftover typing, not the finding.
advisories.suggestedFix: Move the entry out of tags into a sibling key such as companions, so tags is exactly the set classMap draws from.

coordinatorNote: v6 repairs my v5 blocker in substance and both of my SHOULD-FIX items, and the osFamily binding of identifier schemes is a clean piece of work. The problem is that this generation's two structural repairs each carried something away with them. Replacing linux-uname-release with linux-distro-userspace correctly diagnoses that a kernel release is not a host-ABI identity, but the replacement has no normalization — while EXACT-BUILD.equality still compares 'byte-exact canonicalIdentifier after normalization' — no rule for composing its two parts into the single canonicalIdentifier the tag requires, no vocabulary behind the word 'closed', and an open 'or equivalent' escape. That is four independent ways for two verifiers to disagree about the same Linux host, in the required member that gates allowlist freeze, so it is a blocker on the same grounds I blocked the filesystem token at v5. Likewise, moving sonameAbi inside the libc authenticity payload is exactly right, but it is the edit that makes an exclusion rule load-bearing, and the sentence saying companion labels never decide identity was deleted in that same edit, leaving an optional field under an exact-match drift rule. The fstype residue is narrower and I have graded it accordingly, though f_fstypename is a BSD field with no Linux counterpart, so the Linux half of that escape is still unnamed. I have also escalated the ledger-rotation finding from advisory to SHOULD-FIX and said why: v6 deleted the disclosure that was the reason I kept it advisory twice, and left an inherited repair line claiming a naming that no longer exists. DR-126 stays OPEN. No per-OS table is populated, D-096 appears nowhere, and nothing here marks the row SATISFIED, qualifies G22, or authorizes docs/v2/implementation/.
